rationale: Direct peer-reviewed evidence demonstrates that structural central nervous system (CNS) malformations occur in individuals with bi-allelic pathogenic variants in FILIP1. Roos et al. (2023) identified five patients across four consanguineous families presenting with congenital neuromuscular disease accompanied by structural brain malformations, notably periventricular heterotopia (a known cortical migration anomaly consistent with FILIP1's interaction with FLNA). Subsequent independent reports and reviews (Watts et al. 2024, Inoue & Weihl 2025, Seneor et al. 2026) corroborate that CNS structural defects, ranging from neuronal migration anomalies to profound malformations, are part of the FILIP1 phenotypic spectrum. Consequently, normal neuroimaging or the presence of structural CNS anomalies cannot be leveraged as an exclusion criterion when differentiating FILIP1-related disorders from congenital muscular dystrophies or brain-muscle-eye syndromes.

evidence.text: Roos et al. (2023) established that bi-allelic variants in FILIP1 cause a recessive syndromic disorder combining congenital myopathy, dysmorphic features, and neurological manifestations including structural brain malformations such as periventricular heterotopia.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance and specific subtype distribution of structural brain malformations (e.g., periventricular nodular heterotopia vs. pachygyria/lissencephaly vs. corpus callosum dysgenesis) across all molecularly confirmed FILIP1 patients undergoing standardized high-resolution 3T brain MRI?
new_directions.rationale: Although periventricular heterotopia and profound malformations have been reported, systematic neuroradiological re-evaluation is necessary to determine the exact prevalence of subclinical neuronal migration defects.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of structural CNS malformations correlate with variant class (truncating null alleles vs. hypomorphic missense variants altering FLNA binding kinetics)?
new_directions.rationale: FLNA variants specifically cause X-linked periventricular nodular heterotopia; understanding whether FILIP1 variants disrupt FLNA-mediated neuronal migration differentially could explain the phenotypic heterogeneity observed between arthrogryposis-predominant and heterotopia-predominant cohorts.
